beats.text: The villain? The teleop bottleneck. Human experts cannot monitor ninety-six robots simultaneously. Scaling fleets manually is a physical impossibility.
beats.visual_focus: Split screen showing 96 robot feeds with one overwhelmed human operator.

beats.text: Collective Experience Learning turns every failure into a teaching moment. Robots share execution logs to build a common, robust policy.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—I've seen enough robot fail-compilations to know exactly what you're talking about. You didn't waste time with 'Hey guys' or 'In this video,' which is a huge plus. I get the gist of the shared replay buffer, but Beat 4 gets a little hand-wavy. How exactly is it matching failure contexts? Is it just vector similarity search or something more complex? It feels like you're skipping the actual engineering 'how' for a slightly buzzwordy 'what'.

thriller_metadata.physical_analogy: A single human trying to babysit a thousand toddlers simultaneously in a dark room.
thriller_metadata.paradigm_shift: Robots self-correcting through shared failure data without human intervention.
